title: Feather Colour Affect Aggressive Behaviour of Chickens with Same Genotype
author: Changsheng Nie
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ysgfwbw

steps.title: Perform cross to generate F1 hybrids
steps.instruction: Cross male RIR (Rhode Island Red) with female WL (White Leghorn) to obtain F1 hybrids; produce 150 red‑feathered daughters and 150 white‑feathered daughters and randomly select them for experiments; note that all males are white.

steps.title: Collect and hatch eggs, select females
steps.instruction: Incubate eggs from the WL male × RIR female cross simultaneously; after hatching collect red‑ and white‑feathered female chickens (all males are white) for further use.

steps.title: Rear chicks in controlled cages
steps.instruction: Raise red and white hens separately in chick cages (~30 chickens per cage) from day 1 to day 115 under artificial conditions (temperature 23 °C, ventilation fans and cooling pads, photoperiod 13.5 L : 10.5 D from 07:00 to 20:30 with 5 W light power at 26 weeks).

steps.title: Transfer to adult cages and pens
steps.instruction: At day 115 move birds to adult cages (3 chickens per cage); at 20 weeks transfer them to six pens (each 4.30 m × 4.00 m × 2.00 m, 1.00 m above floor) equipped with automatic drinkers, fresh water ad libitum, and manual feeding of standard commercial feed; divide birds into groups: 1 & 2 are red‑hen replicates, 3 & 4 each contain 25 red + 25 white hens (blended groups), 5 & 6 are white‑hen replicates; weigh all birds at 20 weeks and again at 25 weeks.

steps.title: Maintain housing conditions
steps.instruction: Keep the temperature constantly at 23 °C with ventilation fans and cooling pads; maintain the 13.5 L : 10.5 D photoperiod (07:00‑20:30) and 5 W light power throughout the housing period.

steps.title: Allow five‑week adaptation period
steps.instruction: Let all birds acclimate to the new pen conditions for 5 weeks before any behavioural testing.

steps.title: Record aggressive behaviours
steps.instruction: From day 177 to day 181 (26 weeks) monitor each pen between 12:00 and 12:30; one observer records behaviours for 30 min per pen per day over 5 days (30 min × 5 days × 6 pens). Count behaviours separately for attacker and victim for red and white feathers. Record B1 (chase, attack) and B2 (peck, threat) when the following criteria are met: stiff body posture, inter‑bird distance < 0.25 m, head positioned above or below the receiver’s head, and feathers may be lifted. Note that blended groups are 3 and 4.

steps.title: Collect blood and extract DNA
steps.instruction: Obtain wing‑vein blood from red‑ and white‑feathered hens without anesthetic; extract genomic DNA using standard phenol/chloroform protocols.

steps.title: Select sixty females for genotyping
steps.instruction: From the F1 population choose 60 females (29 white, 31 red) for further genetic analysis.

steps.title: Choose SOX10 locus for analysis
steps.instruction: Select loci 3 (SOX10 gene) for genotyping and association analysis; loci 2 (dominant white I and sex‑linked recessive feather Zs) are already known. SOX10 is linked to the dark‑brown (DB) phenotype via a 3 kb deletion upstream of the transcription start site.

steps.title: Set up PCR for SOX10 deletion
steps.instruction: Perform PCR on a Applied Biosystems Veriti 96‑well thermal cycler following the manufacturer’s protocol. Amplify the 8.3 kb upstream deletion of SOX10 using primers: 1F (5’-CCTTTGTCTTAAGGCTCCTCTTT-3’), 1R (5’-CCTTGTGGAGACCAGGTGTT-3’), and 6R (5’-TGCTGAGACATTTGCTGACA-3’). The 1F/1R pair yields a 611 bp fragment (wild‑type db/db allele); the 1F/6R pair yields a 1257 bp fragment (dark‑brown DB/DB allele).

steps.title: Visualise PCR products on agarose gel
steps.instruction: Run the PCR products on an agarose gel to display the 611 bp and 1257 bp fragments corresponding to the wild‑type and dark‑brown alleles, respectively.
